findings.claim: The fix for verify-251 finding 1 covers only a signed_off append that writes no bytes. When it fails after part of its line is on disk (disk full, a lock file replaced mid-write, the head record's staging failing; case.py:1220-1272 raise SaveNotRecorded and keep the torn tail saying 'the next holder confirms dropping it'), the log is torn past the recorded pack_written. Every later sign_off then fails at require_intact (pack.py:648) with CaseLogBroken, and no CLI or workspace path calls CaseLog.drop_torn_entry (grep finds only its definition, case.py:1060). The pack stays with an evidence.json sign-off the log never records, and the snapshot cannot be signed off with the tool: the same dead end the escalation named for 'SaveNotRecorded from a full disk'. The new test test_r42_a_sign_off_entry_not_recorded_can_be_recorded_again replaces CaseLog.append outright, so it never covers a partly written line, and the claim's 'not_reproduced' disposition overreaches.
findings.repro: Build a case and preview; make the head record's staging write raise OSError(ENOSPC) only during the signed_off append (for example, patch os.open on the head's temporary file once pack_written is recorded); call pack.sign_off: SaveNotRecorded, and caselog.for_case(folder).verify() reports a torn entry at the signed_off position. Call pack.sign_off again with the same name: CaseLogBroken(torn=True). `cma case sign` exits 3, the workspace answers 409 'Nothing can be signed off until it is resolved', and no command resolves it.

findings.claim: _sync_dir(packs) runs after os.rename and outside the try/except that removes the pack folder, so a failed folder fsync leaves packs/<snapshot> in place with no pack_written entry. The OSError reaches _case_errors, which prints 'nothing was recorded in the case', and the next sign-off asks the user to move the folder aside by hand. This contradicts the module's stated rule that the log and the folder agree.
findings.repro: Patch pack._sync_dir so it raises OSError(EIO) when called with the packs folder (the second call); call sign_off: OSError, packs/<snapshot> exists, and no pack_written entry is logged; a second sign_off raises SignOffRefused '... records no pack written for it ... move that folder aside'.
